classification.difficultyReason: Adjust the union for the shared students and take its complement, then use the Chinese-student total as the denominator in the conditional part.

content.prompt: In a class of 30 students, 18 study Chinese, 15 study Japanese and 6 study both of these subjects. If a student is chosen at random from the class, find the probability that the student

answer.worked:
The six students who study both are counted twice in $18+15$, so $18+15-6=27$ students study at least one of the two subjects. This leaves $30-27=3$ students who study neither.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{neither})&=\frac{3}{30}\\P(\text{neither})&=\frac{1}{10}\end{align*}$$

children.prompt: studies Japanese, given that they also study Chinese.

answer.short:
$\frac{1}{3}$

Use the 18 Chinese students as the sample space.
answer.worked:
Of the 18 students who study Chinese, 6 also study Japanese.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{Japanese}\mid\text{Chinese})&=\frac{6}{18}\\P(\text{Japanese}\mid\text{Chinese})&=\frac{1}{3}\end{align*}$$
